original_value: AbstractLearning knowledge graph (KG) embeddings is an emerging technique for a variety of downstream tasks such as summarization, link prediction, information retrieval, and question answering. However, most existing KG embedding models neglect space and, therefore, do not perform well when applied to (geo)spatial data and tasks. Most models that do consider space primarily rely on some notions of distance. These models suffer from higher computational complexity during training while still losing information beyond the relative distance between entities. In this work, we propose a location‐aware KG embedding model called SE‐KGE. It directly encodes spatial information such as point coordinates or bounding boxes of geographic entities into the KG embedding space. The resulting model is capable of handling different types of spatial reasoning. We also construct a geographic knowledge graph as well as a set of geographic query–answer pairs called DBGeo to evaluate the performance of SE‐KGE in comparison to multiple baselines. Evaluation results show that SE‐KGE outperforms these baselines on the DBGeo data set for the geographic logic query answering task. This demonstrates the effectiveness of our spatially‐explicit model and the importance of considering the scale of different geographic entities. Finally, we introduce a novel downstream task called spatial semantic lifting which links an arbitrary location in the study area to entities in the KG via some relations. Evaluation on DBGeo shows that our model outperforms the baseline by a substantial margin.

result.paraphrase: AbstractLearning knowledge graph (KG) embeddings is an emerging method for diverse downstream applications, including summarization, link prediction, information retrieval, and question answering. Yet most current KG embedding models ignore space and therefore work poorly for (geo)spatial data and tasks. The models that do account for space mostly depend on distance-based notions, which increase training complexity while still discarding information beyond the relative distance between entities. In this paper, we present a location-aware KG embedding model, SE-KGE, that directly encodes spatial information such as point coordinates or bounding boxes of geographic entities into the KG embedding space. As a result, it can handle different forms of spatial reasoning. We also build a geographic knowledge graph and a set of geographic query-answer pairs, DBGeo, to assess SE-KGE against multiple baselines. The evaluation shows that SE-KGE outperforms these baselines on DBGeo for geographic logic query answering, highlighting both the effectiveness of our spatially explicit model and the importance of considering the scale of different geographic entities. Finally, we propose a new downstream task, spatial semantic lifting, which links an arbitrary location in the study area to KG entities through relations. Results on DBGeo show that our model exceeds the baseline by a wide margin.
